invariants: One creature exists per creation. Its initial drawing, persistent identity, and hidden seed remain the same throughout its lifetime; no breeding, offspring or multi-generational progression.

The game uses a real phylogenetic reference as a branching map of possible developmental forms for the SAME creature over time. The observed affinity/path may progress, but is not literal taxonomic evolution or scientific ancestry-changing.

Scientific taxonomy and fictional extensions have distinct, inspectable provenance.

Every agent reads this plan before touching the engine, updates task status and acceptance tests together.
Product temporal contract: a physical anatomical change may commit only at T_k=hatchAtMs+k*86400000 for k=1..365, never between checks or after maturity; zero-change outcomes are valid.
The former forced 30-day lifespan and hourly/8192-hour anatomy are retired. Historical numerical evidence is explicitly legacy; only the daily timeline defines production anatomy.

Infipet must support a broad, independently verifiable space of anatomical transformations. No implementation may preserve physical correctness by reducing development to predominantly linear extensions, branches, or cosmetic changes.

Developmental variety must emerge from the player's authored material, permanent genetic potential, deterministic chaotic processes, anatomical constraints, and chronological care. The system must demonstrate genuine variation in whole-body proportions, topology, tissue distribution, structural specialization, and developmental trajectories, without predetermined creature outcomes. An individual organism may legitimately remain unchanged or favor one developmental strategy. System-wide capability must not collapse to a narrow family of outcomes.
Morphological expressiveness is coequal with source continuity and physical material conservation; display-only warps, pose, or pigment cannot count as physically achieved anatomical diversity.

agentCoordination.writeOwnership: One algorithm owner writes each owned path; all other agents treat it as read-only. Shared imports are allowed. Owner boundaries are routing rules, not permission constraints.
agentCoordination.parallelExecution: Agents can develop algorithms concurrently against existing typed public interfaces. Cross-algorithm API changes require interface proposals to the integration owner before editing shared runtime files.
agentCoordination.taskLifecycle: Agent selects one task ID, reads acceptance contract and ownedPaths, writes smallest targeted test, implements algorithm, runs that test, updates status in same commit.
agentCoordination.integrationGate: Integration agent alone edits App.tsx, src/lineage/index.ts or src/simulation/growth.ts while separate algorithm work is in progress.
agentCoordination.testConvention: Every new algorithm-local test must be named tests/alg-<algorithmId>-<feature>.test.ts, be referenced in roadmap/plan.json and measure that feature only.
agentCoordination.reporting: Prefer booleans, numeric hashes, invariants and narrow metric summaries; never commit screenshot batches, historical build logs or generated test matrices.

singleCreatureLifecycle.unitOfSimulation: one continuously identifiable organism across its entire lifetime
singleCreatureLifecycle.creation: one authored drawing plus one once-assigned alphanumeric random seed
singleCreatureLifecycle.genotype: per-pet fixed developmental potential; no mating, meiosis, gametes, parent genomes, genetic recombination, offspring or inheritance across pets
singleCreatureLifecycle.progression: The same pet may undergo dramatic, constrained anatomical changes at no more than 365 real-time daily check boundaries (one per elapsed 24h from hatch/birth), with actual recorded care influencing each check; its mature physical anatomy is fixed after check 365. Physiological play continues independently.
singleCreatureLifecycle.phylogeny: the scientific tree supplies hierarchical anatomical constraints and branching possibilities for single-pet developmental trajectories; stage affinities along its branches may change, but this is a game developmental metaphor, not a claim that an individual changes its actual scientific ancestry

terminology.phylogeneticAncestor: a reference node in a biological taxonomy, not a parent pet
terminology.phylogeneticDescendant: a reference taxon descended in the real tree of life, never offspring produced by this pet
terminology.inheritedGenome: stable latent individual traits assigned at creation, not traits passed to children
terminology.evolutionaryPath: one creature's sequential changes over time, not multiple generations or population evolution

anatomicalDevelopment.authority: APPROVED PRODUCT SPECIFICATION; implemented by the production daily material timeline. Historical hour-named numerical helpers do not define the player clock.
anatomicalDevelopment.unitOfGrowth: one discrete physical-development opportunity each 86400000 elapsed milliseconds
anatomicalDevelopment.anchor: the individual pet's persisted clock.hatchAtMs (the moment a live organism hatches or is born); incubation does not consume a daily check
anatomicalDevelopment.checkTime: T_k = hatchAtMs + k*86400000, for integer 1 <= k <= 365, using safe integer UTC epoch milliseconds; not local midnight or calendar dates
anatomicalDevelopment.careWindows: Check k consumes only recorded chronological history on [T_(k-1), T_k); a command exactly at T_k belongs to the NEXT care window; no future observations or invented care while away
anatomicalDevelopment.anatomicalState: A(t)=A_0 for 0 <= t < T_1; A(t)=A_k for T_k <= t < T_(k+1) (1 <= k < 365); A(t)=A_365 for all t >= T_365, while alive. Each A_k is one verified fully physical graph
anatomicalDevelopment.checkOperation: A_k=F(A_(k-1),immutable birth drawing, fixed genotype, permanent chaotic seed/state, valid physical operators, summarized actual care window k, chronological resource bounds). Any F may be a physically constrained identity/null
anatomicalDevelopment.invariant: All new, removed, or relocated anatomical cells/tissues/links originate in explicit material transactions at exactly T_k; no anatomical mutations at fractional/hourly times, in renderer, or after T_365
anatomicalDevelopment.timelineTime: Use elapsed 24h intervals, including time zone/DST changes; app sessions, reopening, preview scrubbing and render frames cannot trigger extra checks
anatomicalDevelopment.missedChecks: On return, replay due check indices in ascending order using recorded evidence and the game's actual absent-state effects; no fabricated player commands, no batch leap that skips a check, at most 365 lifetime physical checks
anatomicalDevelopment.snapshots: Memoize the last validated completed check by persistent birth/genome/care-prefix identity; deterministic fresh replay from authored birth must reproduce every material transaction and graph exactly
anatomicalDevelopment.independentGameplay: Physiology, needs, care, death from legitimate gameplay causes, animation, locomotion, pose and surface appearance may continue between/after checks; none may silently mutate physical anatomy
anatomicalDevelopment.lifePolicy: The forced 30-day lifespan is removed. Actual care and physiological mortality remain; healthy pets survive through check 365 and afterward with permanently mature anatomy.
anatomicalDevelopment.offlineClock: Persist historical birth and event times; reject backward / impossible timestamps and replay deterministically; local-only time cannot fully prevent device-clock tampering without a trusted server, so never promise tamper proof offline
anatomicalDevelopment.legacyStatus: Historical 512h/720h/8192h primitive tests are explicitly legacy numerical coverage. Former hourly performance gates are retired; production qualification is the 365-opportunity daily suite.

morphologicalExpressiveness.principle: Infipet must support a broad, independently verifiable space of anatomical transformations. No implementation may preserve physical correctness by reducing development to predominantly linear extensions, branches, or cosmetic changes.
morphologicalExpressiveness.systemLevelRequirement: Developmental variety must emerge from the player's authored material, permanent genetic potential, deterministic chaotic processes, anatomical constraints, and chronological care. The system must demonstrate genuine variation in whole-body proportions, topology, tissue distribution, structural specialization, and developmental trajectories, without predetermined creature outcomes. An individual organism may legitimately remain unchanged or favor one developmental strategy. System-wide capability must not collapse to a narrow family of outcomes.
